title: RBCTest: Leveraging LLMs to Mine and Verify Oracles of API Response Bodies for RESTful API Testing
summary: The original RBCTest pipeline automatically mines constraints from OpenAPI specifications and generates test cases to detect mismatches in real REST API responses. It operates in three phases: (1) Constraint Mining — an LLM reads the OAS spec and a real API response to identify two constraint types: Response Property (RP) constraints on field schemas (type, enum, URI format, nullable) and Request-Response (RR) constraints where a request parameter determines a response field value; (2) Test Generation — the LLM generates Python verification scripts for each mined constraint; (3) Test Execution — scripts are executed against real responses and verdicts are collected. The original pipeline uses GPT-4o with an Observation-Confirmation (OC) two-step prompting scheme and reports results averaged over 5 independent runs.

This reproduction replaces all LLM phases with a single Claude Sonnet 4.6 call that takes the OAS spec and one real API response and outputs both constraint types in one structured JSON response. Two prompt strategies are evaluated: Prompt A (black-box, provides the output schema and a few-shot example but no explicit reasoning steps) and Prompt B (chain-of-thought, adds 9 explicit reasoning steps covering spec reading, property observation, RR identification, script generation, and output formatting). The pipeline runs on 9 of the 11 AGORA+ benchmark services — the 2 GitHub services are excluded because their OAS specs are ~460K tokens each, exceeding the 190K token context limit.

dataset.name: AGORA+ benchmark
dataset.exclusion_reason: OAS specs ~1.6MB (~460K tokens) each, exceeding 190K token context limit

metric_note: Macro-averaged P/R/F1 across 9 services; constraint match key is (operation, response_resource, attribute) triple; RP and RR constraints evaluated together (RQ1 only).
